title: Flat Client Orchestration (Flat Two-Tier Bloat)
pattern: Orchestrating multi-service sequences and state updates directly inside client code (mobile, web, CLI) rather than behind a server-side gateway or manager service.
why_bad: The clients become tightly coupled to the internal service layout. If a backend service is updated or rewritten, all client applications must be updated and deployed concurrently. This causes client duplication and makes database/service migrations extremely risky [54, 55, 541].
detection: Client-facing codebases performing multiple sequential write mutations across separate downstream service endpoints.
counterexample: Valid for simple applications where only one client exists and backend services are stable. Mark as `Context-dependent`.
fix: Introduce a backend Coordinator or Manager service that encapsulates the orchestration sequence, exposing a single unified endpoint to clients [54, 55].
source: Righting Software, Chapter 2, "Decomposition - Clients Bloat and Coupling" [54, 55, 541]
